text:
maya: Hey team, incoming from Acme - their Dedicated pool dc-prod-4 started returning 429s and timeouts when clients send long-context requests (~60-80k tokens). Customer reports sudden token billing spike too. Can we triage?
noah: Request id req_9e3fa7b, saw first 429 at 2024-06-10T22:13:05Z. Most requests are streaming chat with really long histories.
support-bot: Created escalation ticket DEVOPS-9892 for dc-prod-4 (auto-tag: kvcache-pressure). :spiral_notepad:
liam: @maya @oliver looking. Quick check: which model variant and average seq len distribution?
maya: Model: open-llm-xl-16g, quantized; seq len tail ~65k, median ~3k. Dedicated pool is single-tenant-ish but shares node pools with burst tenants.
oliver: Pulled node logs around timestamp. kvcache eviction rate spike and slab compaction thrash. Snippet: ```[2024-06-10T22:13:05Z] kvcache: evict_keys=12543 evict_bytes=3.1GB long_context=true slab_reclaim=high
[2024-06-10T22:13:06Z] autoscaler: scale_up_requested=true reason=kv_pressure
[2024-06-10T22:13:07Z] kvcache: compaction_failed=1 err=ENOMEM```
liam: Oof. That ENOMEM during compaction suggests fragmentation not just raw usage. Which explains throttle gating firing.
maya: Customer says autoscaler took ~45s before new nodes came online and throttle policy started rejecting. They had burst traffic too.
noah: I ran a quick scrape of pool metrics: fragments=842, evictions/sec=12.4k, kv_free=120MB at 22:13:10Z.
oliver: kv_free that low + high fragments == hot eviction churn. Per-tenant throttle kicks in to protect node stability -> 429s. Also billing spike comes from clients resending when they see 429.
sophie: Is there a short-term mitigation we can offer the customer while infra investigates?
liam: Temporary mitigations: 1) enable burst capacity override for dc-prod-4 2) suggest customer pin to shorter context variant or smaller model 3) enable prefix/KV cache TTL extension for this tenant.
maya: I applied burst override for dc-prod-4: `POST /admin/pools/dc-prod-4/override {"burst_enabled":true,"burst_tokens":200000}` — customer reports 429s dropped to near-zero but tail latency spiked for ~30s. :thumbsup:
oliver: Good emergency step. For root cause we need to reproduce in staging and gather vmem fragmentation profile. Please run the kv profiler: `rwi-kv-prof --node node-12.dc-prod --duration 60 --out /tmp/kv-prof.json`. Also collect slab map: `curl http://node-12.internal/metrics | grep slab`
noah: Running now, output partial: `fragments=842, evict_rate=12450, slab_reassign_fail=3`
liam: That slab_reassign_fail matches compaction_failed in logs. Plan: schedule node-level compaction patch + reduce slab_min_free threshold in next deploy. I'll open infra change with rollback window.
maya: Can we also add a short-term route rule to send extremely long contexts to a compatible model variant with smaller KV footprint? Customer is open to that.
sophie: Product note: we should add an auto-suggestion in Console when long-context workloads are detected (hint: model variant, cache TTLs, burst). Filing UX ticket.
oliver: For troubleshooting steps: 1) repro in staging with longctx-regen script (I pushed script to infra-tools) 2) capture kv-prof and heap profile 3) run compaction-targeted job 4) test autoscale responsiveness (measure time from scale_up_request -> node_ready).
liam: Command to repro in staging: `python tools/longctx-regen.py --tokens 65000 --concurrency 6 --target pool=staging-dc1`
maya: I'll coordinate with customer for a repro window tomorrow 02:00 UTC and collect request ids.
support-bot: Escalation DEVOPS-9892 updated: assigned -> liam, severity -> high.
liam: I'll take ownership of the infra fix and keep updates here. Next actions: repro in staging, run kv profiler, open infra PR to adjust compaction thresholds, and follow up with customer about routing options.
maya: Thanks all — I'll post customer confirmation and logs once I have them. :eyes:
